pairs.subject: candidate-archetype-routing
pairs.evidence: app/_components/results/ArchetypeBanner.tsx:114 "Save as profile" sends the pipeline's INFERRED archetype back as the candidate's self-declaration. pipeline/jobfit/registry.py:300-306 then gives it the 0.9 declaration tier and the reason "self-declared: X", so a 0.4 needs-review routing (including the no-signal default to bau) is saved as a confident declaration the candidate never made, and its review flag is gone. This is the laundered-declaration failure the standard names.

techniques.evidence: app/_components/results/ArchetypeBanner.tsx:114 The code comment at :106-107 says it pins the inferred archetype as the self-declaration so the re-route is deterministic. The technique says to pin a derived class as derived and never re-submit an inference as self-declared.

app/_components/results/ArchetypeBanner.tsx:133 The below-threshold review flag shows as its own chip. Confidence is relabelled "signals agree" (a vote share, per the :81-88 comment), and an absent value is left out rather than shown as 0%. It is still printed as an NN% figure.
app/_components/results/ArchetypeBanner.tsx:173 The banner shows the signals that fired next to the class, so the recruiter sees the explanation and not just a verdict.

app/_components/results/ArchetypeBanner.tsx:77 An archetype the registry does not know renders as "Unrouted" and is never turned into a concrete class. This only covers the sentinel the banner receives. The no-signal case arrives from upstream already labelled bau (see notes).

pairs.subject: candidate-archetype-routing
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/archetypes.ts:21 The TS side reads the same archetypes.json the Python pipeline imports, builds the shield set from its flag, validates weight vectors on read and on write with Python's exact 1e-6 tolerance (lockstep test), archives entries instead of deleting them, and fails the shield closed for unknown ids while keeping isEarlyCareer false for them.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/archetypes.ts:21 One declarative file is read by both runtimes. Supporting evidence: protected set derived from the flag (:75), keys canonicalised (:84-86), archive rather than delete (archetype-registry.ts:368-383), and archetype-registry-lockstep.test.ts pins the mirrored constants. Caveat: the static import is cast at :38 without validation, but live decisions go through archetype-live.ts, which validates.

app/_lib/archetype-registry.ts:261 Weights must sum to 1 within 1e-6, each weight must lie in [0,1], and every slot needs a dimension label. This is checked at the write boundary and again when the registry is read (validateRegistry :125-146). In the registry, early-career entries are renamed Foundation/Potential/Fit. I found no scored golden set in this context.

app/_lib/archetypes.ts:121 Unknown means protected for the shield, while isEarlyCareer (:128-130) treats unknown as not early for wording, and both directions are written down. archetypeDisplayKey renders it as "unrouted", and RESERVED_IDS (archetype-registry.ts:50) stops anyone registering the sentinel as a class.
